_comment: The merge gate for `main`, mirrored from the GitHub Ruleset.
This file is the reviewable source of truth for the gate.  The
Ruleset in the GitHub repository settings is applied from it, so
a change to the gate is a change to this file and a pull request,
not a click in the web UI that leaves no trace.
Apply it with:
python tools/apply_ci_ruleset.py --apply
The gate and the CI matrix have to agree, and `check_ci_ruleset.py`
is what says they do.  A required check that no workflow produces
blocks every merge, forever, with nothing to fix from the PR page;
a check the matrix produces but the gate does not require costs
runner time and catches nothing.  That is why the check compares
the two sets for equality rather than for containment.
The Ruleset id is 27017055 and it is named
`protect-main-and-releases` in the repository settings; the name is
historical -- the ruleset now covers `main` only.  See the note on
`conditions.ref_name.include` below for why the release branches
are not covered.
name: protect-main-and-releases

_comment: `main` only.
The ruleset used to cover `refs/heads/release/*` as well, and
that combination was unusable: `ci.yml` and `interop.yml`
declare `pull_request: branches: [main]`, which filters on the
PR's *base* branch, so a pull request into `release/1.1`
triggered neither workflow.  Measured: such a PR reported zero
checks and was `blocked`, while a direct push was refused with
"Changes must be made through a pull request".  The release
branches therefore could not be updated at all -- while
RELEASING.md 3.2 requires hot-fixes to be cherry-picked onto
`release/X.Y`.
The release branches are frozen release lines that receive
cherry-picked hot-fixes by a maintainer.  They do not take
unreviewed pushes, and the full matrix was never satisfiable
there.  `main` is the branch that merges every day, and that is
where the gate belongs.

rules._comment: The protected branch cannot be deleted.
No force-push: the history is the evidence.

_comment: `required_approving_review_count` is 0, and it has to stay 0
until the repository has a second account that can approve.
The repository is owned by a personal account (`NimRTC`) with
exactly one collaborator, so GitHub does not count the
author's own approval: raising this to 1 would make every
pull request permanently unmergeable.
The same argument applies to `require_last_push_approval`
(it demands an approval from somebody who is not the
pusher) and to `require_code_owner_review` (the teams in
CODEOWNERS -- `@nimrtc/maintainers`, `@nimrtc/agent-*` -- do
not exist in a personal-account repository).
`required_review_thread_resolution` is on: a review comment
left unresolved is not a review that happened.
The eleven checks the CI matrix produces on `main` and on
every pull request into `main`.
Strict mode is on: the pull request head has to be up to date
with the base, or a PR can merge on the checks of a commit
that is no longer an ancestor of `main`.
`windows / fast` is deliberately absent.  It comes from
`ci-fast.yml`, which does not run on `main`
(`branches-ignore: [main, 'release/**']`), so requiring it
would block every merge forever.
